title: Release workflow blocked: GHA cannot create PRs
description:
Failing run: https://github.com/OskarHulter/oh-monorepo/actions/runs/24941927293

Error: 'GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests' (HttpError from changesets/action when opening Version PR).

Root cause: repo-level setting Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests' is OFF. API: can_approve_pull_request_reviews=false.

Fix: PUT repos/OskarHulter/oh-monorepo/actions/permissions/workflow with can_approve_pull_request_reviews=true. Keep default_workflow_permissions=read (release.yml already opts-in to pull-requests: write per-job, principle of least privilege preserved). Re-run failed workflow.
close_reason: Flipped repo setting can_approve_pull_request_reviews=true via gh api. Re-ran failed run 24941927293 — green in 21s. Version PR #9 (changeset-release/main → main) now open. default_workflow_permissions kept at 'read'; release.yml continues to opt-in to pull-requests: write per-job.

title: RFC: @oh/client refactor — kernel + ui barrel + ports & adapters
description: Refactor RFC for the @oh/client package. Output of the deepening drill on candidate 3 during website-tracer research. Sets the public API shape, file layout, ports schema, discipline rules, and migration steps. Hybrid spine: ports/adapters with consumer-owned <App>; cosmos via fixture adapter.
notes:
# Context

Ticket emerged from the improve-codebase-architecture skill drill on the
website-tracer research (docs/plans/website-tracer/research.md). Candidate 3
"single deep package, deliberately few exports" was selected; four parallel
designs were explored; final pick is a hybrid:

- Design 4 (Ports & Adapters) as the structural spine.
- Design 3's small-default-tier ergonomics, refined: <App> stays consumer-owned;
  @oh/client exports <Providers> instead.

# Public surface

@oh/client (kernel):
- <Providers ports={...}>      # umbrella; composes Telemetry/Router/Theme/Data context
- usePorts()                    # read ports inside lib + consumer
- Port types: TelemetryPort, RouterPort, ThemePort, DataPort, Ports

@oh/client/ui (UI surface):
- Components: Hero, SocialLinks, Button, layout primitives, ... (re-exported from ./components)
- Features (hooks): useSocialLinks, ... (re-exported from ./features)

@oh/client/ui/styles.css      # Tailwind v4 entry — only stylesheet in the package

@oh/client/adapters/fixture   # createFixturePorts(seed); only adapter shipped

Concrete adapters (R2 / DuckDB / Sentry / Better-Auth / Tanstack Router) live in
apps/website/src/adapters/. Library never imports concrete infra.

# package.json exports (high barrels only)

{
  "exports": {
    ".":                  { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",                "import": "./dist/index.mjs" },
    "./ui":               { "types": "./dist/ui/index.d.ts",             "import": "./dist/ui/index.mjs" },
    "./ui/styles.css":    "./dist/ui/styles.css",
    "./adapters/fixture": { "types": "./dist/adapters/fixture/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/adapters/fixture/index.mjs" }
  }
}

Four public entries. Deeper paths (./ui/components/button) are private; internal
barrels exist for cosmos + for the public ./ui to re-export from.

# File layout

packages/client/
  cosmos.config.ts               # at package root by convention; rootDir: 'src/ui'
  src/
    index.ts                     # core kernel
    ports.ts                     # cross-cutting port types
    providers.tsx                # <Providers> umbrella
    ui/
      index.ts                   # high barrel — re-exports components/, features/
      styles.css
      components/
        button/{button.tsx, button.fixture.tsx}
        hero/{hero.tsx, hero.fixture.tsx}
        social-links/{social-links.tsx, social-links.fixture.tsx}
        index.ts                 # internal barrel
      features/
        social-links/
          use-social-links.ts
          port.ts                # feature-specific data port
          fixture.ts             # fixture impl
        index.ts                 # internal barrel
    adapters/
      fixture/index.ts           # createFixturePorts(seed)

# Ports schema (initial)

src/ports.ts:

  import type { SocialLinksPort } from './ui/features/social-links/port'

  export interface TelemetryPort {
    event(name: string, attrs?: Record<string, unknown>): void
    error(err: unknown, attrs?: Record<string, unknown>): void
    span<T>(name: string, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>
  }
  export interface RouterPort {
    push(to: string): void
    useParams<T extends Record<string, string>>(): T
    Link: React.ComponentType<{ to: string; children: React.ReactNode }>
  }
  export interface ThemePort { mode: 'light' | 'dark' | 'system'; toggle(): void }
  export interface DataPort  { socialLinks: SocialLinksPort /* + future features */ }
  export interface Ports     { telemetry: TelemetryPort; router: RouterPort; theme: ThemePort; data: DataPort }

Cross-cutting ports stay at core; feature-specific data ports live with the feature; DataPort umbrella imports them.

# Discipline rules (oxlint via vp lint)

no-restricted-imports rule:
- src/ui/** and src/ui/features/** MUST NOT import: @sentry/*, @tanstack/react-router, @duckdb/*, @cloudflare/*, raw fetch URLs.
- Only src/adapters/fixture/** + apps/website/src/adapters/** may import concrete infra.
- @oh/client/ui/styles.css is the only CSS entry in the package. No component-level CSS imports.

# Build strategy

V1: TS-source exports (mirror @oh/shared pattern). package.json exports point to
src/ paths in dev; dist paths in published builds. No vp pack in dev loop.
- Pro: faster dev, no build step gating cosmos / app dev server.
- Con: consumers must transpile our TS. Acceptable since current consumers are
  in-monorepo and run vite-plus.

Defer vp pack multi-entry to a follow-up when @oh/client gets published externally.
If R1 (website-tracer) needs the build path sooner, revisit then.

# Cosmos config

cosmos.config.ts at packages/client/ root with:
- rootDir: 'src/ui'
- componentPaths: ['src/ui/components/**', 'src/ui/features/**']
- fixturesDir: '__fixtures__' OR file pattern *.fixture.tsx (lean: file pattern, co-located)
- decorator: <Providers ports={createFixturePorts(seed)}> auto-wraps every fixture

# Consumer wiring (apps/website example)

// apps/website/src/app.tsx
import { Providers } from '@oh/client'
import { Hero, SocialLinks } from '@oh/client/ui'
import '@oh/client/ui/styles.css'
import { ports } from './adapters'

export function App() {
  return (
    <Providers ports={ports}>
      <Hero />
      <SocialLinks />
    </Providers>
  )
}

// apps/website/src/adapters/index.ts
import { createFixturePorts } from '@oh/client/adapters/fixture'
import { createTanstackRouterPort } from './router'
import { createSentryTelemetry } from './sentry'

const fixture = createFixturePorts({ /* seed */ })
export const ports = {
  ...fixture,                                  // start fully fixture-backed for MVP
  router: createTanstackRouterPort(),          // swap real adapters as they ship
  telemetry: createSentryTelemetry({ dsn: import.meta.env.SENTRY_DSN }),
}

# Migration plan from current stub

Current state: packages/client/src/index.ts is a stub (export function fn());
single export entry; vite.config.ts uses vp pack with dts.tsgo + exports:true.

Steps (each is a separate beads issue, see linked-from):
1. Replace src/index.ts stub with kernel: ports.ts, providers.tsx, index.ts
   re-exporting <Providers>, usePorts, port types.
2. Scaffold src/ui/{components,features}/ with internal barrels.
3. Add Tailwind v4 to the package (devDep), src/ui/styles.css with @import "tailwindcss".
4. Add adapters/fixture with createFixturePorts.
5. Update package.json exports map to the 4 high-barrel entries pointing at
   src/ paths (TS-source) for v1.
6. Wire oxlint no-restricted-imports rule in packages/client/.
7. Wire cosmos.config.ts; add one fixture per scaffolded component.
8. Migrate apps/website to consume Providers + ui (after R1 spike resolves
   tanstack-start/vp compatibility).

# Cross-references

- docs/plans/website-tracer/research.md (this drill's source)
- oh-monorepo-su7 (react-cosmos adoption)
- oh-monorepo-jn4 (Sentry → TelemetryPort adapter)
- oh-monorepo-te9 (Better-Auth → future port)
- oh-monorepo-b4b (DuckDB-WASM → DataPort adapter later)
- oh-monorepo-ctc (Convex vs DO → DataPort adapter later)
- oh-monorepo-cgt (Tailwind v4 + animation/shaders)
- oh-monorepo-tfx (CF-only area; CF Pages target for the consumer app)

# Open questions deferred to implementation

- Cosmos fixture pattern: file-suffix (*.fixture.tsx) vs __fixtures__/ — lean file-suffix.
- Does <Providers> mount React Query / Suspense / ErrorBoundary by default, or are those consumer-owned too? Lean: consumer-owned in v1; revisit if every consumer ends up duplicating.
- Tailwind v4 config: in packages/client/ for the lib's @theme tokens, OR consumed entirely from apps/website? Lean: tokens live with the styles.css in the lib so the design system is self-contained.

# Acceptance criteria

- @oh/client builds with the new exports map.
- apps/website (post R1) consumes Providers + Hero + SocialLinks via the documented pattern.
- A single landing page renders with createFixturePorts only — no real adapters wired.
- Cosmos opens at least one fixture per shipped component without depending on consumer adapters.
- vp lint --type-aware passes; oxlint discipline rule blocks a deliberate violation in a test fixture.
R1 (Tanstack Start RC + vp compat) resolved GREEN in PR #11. apps/website-spike/ build + dev both succeed; vite-plus 0.1.19 (Vite 8.0.8) honors the tanstackStart + nitro + viteReact + tailwindcss plugin chain without patching. No plain-Vite fallback needed for v1. See docs/plans/website-tracer/r1-spike-notes.md.

title: Security scanning stack: Dependabot + Trivy + Socket.dev (vs Snyk free)
description: Cover dependency vulns, container scans, IaC scans, supply-chain risk at /bin/zsh. Snyk free tier covered as fallback only. Goal: every PR scanned, no manual gates.
notes:
Stack:
- Dependabot (GH-native): dependency updates + alerts on vulnerable deps. Auto-PRs with grouping.
- CodeQL (GH-native): SAST for JS/TS.
- Trivy: container + IaC + filesystem scans in CI.
- OSV-Scanner (Google, OSS): cross-ecosystem vuln check.
- Socket.dev (free tier): supply-chain risk scoring per dependency, PR comments on risky additions.

Snyk free tier (fallback / consolidated dashboard option):
- Public repos: unlimited tests.
- Private repos: ~200 tests/month for SCA (verify at sign-up; tier may shift).
- Heavy CLI; chatty IDE plugin.
- Adopt only if a single dashboard becomes worth the weight.

Workflows:
1) Weekly Dependabot PR triage; auto-merge patch updates after CI green.
2) PR-time gate: CodeQL + Trivy must pass; Socket.dev posts risk comment.
3) New dependency review: Socket.dev score must clear threshold.
4) Container image scan on each Dockerfile change (Trivy).

Open questions:
- License-compatibility check tooling (FOSSA free tier? license-checker CLI?).
- SBOM generation (Syft) cadence: per release or per main commit.
- Critical vuln response SLA documented somewhere.

title: Web perf monitoring stack: Lighthouse CI + WebPageTest + Web Vitals beacon
description: Cover synthetic + RUM perf at /bin/zsh. Skip SpeedCurve. Lighthouse CI runs per-PR with budgets; WebPageTest API for ground truth on key pages; Web Vitals beacon to PostHog (or Sentry) for real-user data.
notes:
Stack:
- Lighthouse CI in GitHub Actions; budget thresholds checked per PR; static report uploaded as artifact.
- WebPageTest API (free tier) for nightly key-page runs from multiple regions.
- web-vitals npm package; beacon CLS/INP/LCP/FID to PostHog (custom event) and Sentry (release health context).
- Sitespeed.io self-host as alt synthetic if WPT free tier too tight.
- Unlighthouse for periodic site-wide audits.

Budgets (initial, tune later):
- LCP p75 < 2.5s.
- INP p75 < 200ms.
- CLS p75 < 0.1.
- JS bundle < 200kb gzipped on landing.

Workflows:
1) PR perf gate: Lighthouse CI fails build on budget breach.
2) Weekly review: WPT runs + PostHog Web Vitals dashboard.
3) Regression triage: link Web Vitals beacon → Sentry release → suspect commit.

Skipped:
- SpeedCurve: paid only; coverage above replicates 80% at $0.
- DebugBear / Calibre: paid; revisit if budget appears.

Open questions:
- Where to host LHCI server (or use ephemeral artifact only).
- WPT free tier run limits acceptable.
- Sample rate for Web Vitals beacon (100% on landing, 10% elsewhere).

title: Cloudflare platform inventory + AWS↔CF mapping (adoption stages)
description: Document the full Cloudflare service surface used / planned, with AWS equivalents and the stage at which each gets adopted. Living reference for backend infra decisions.
notes:
Mapping table:
| AWS              | CF                     | Stage     |
| CloudFormation   | Terraform/OpenTofu CF provider OR Pulumi (no native CFN) | when >2 services exist |
| S3               | R2                     | now (parquet store)    |
| Lambda           | Workers                | now                    |
| Lambda (heavy)   | Containers             | when CPU/mem outgrow Workers |
| SQS              | Queues                 | first event-driven worker |
| SNS (fanout)     | Queues w/ multi-consumer; Email Workers; webhooks | as needed |
| CloudWatch       | Logpush + Analytics Engine + Workers Observability | bridged to SigNoz |
| WAF Bot Control  | Bot Management (paid) + Super Bot Fight Mode + Turnstile | when bot lane lights up |
| RDS / Aurora     | Neon/Supabase + Hyperdrive (no native managed PG) | when Postgres needed |
| ElastiCache      | KV (eventually-consistent) or DO storage | per workload |
| DynamoDB         | KV or D1 or DO storage | small relational → D1 |
| Step Functions   | Workflows              | when multi-step batch arrives |
| Kinesis          | Pipelines              | when streaming ingest from ML pipeline |
| OpenSearch       | Vectorize (vector only) + ClickHouse for full-text | per workload |
| SageMaker        | Workers AI (small models) | as needed |

Stage gates:
1) Now (website MVP): Workers, R2, KV, Pages.
2) First backend chunk: Queues, Workflows, Hyperdrive (if Postgres), Drizzle on D1.
3) High-volume ingest: Pipelines, Analytics Engine, Containers.
4) Public API surface: Unkey on Workers, WAF rules.
5) Bot research lane: Bot Management or Turnstile.

Open questions:
- Workers paid plan threshold and budget.
- R2 egress pricing model verified at adoption time.
- Container plan availability + cold-start budget.
- Analytics Engine retention vs SigNoz overlap.

DESIGNATED: This ticket is the CLOUDFLARE-ONLY AREA. All CF-native services + adoption stages live here. Non-CF alternatives are tracked on their own tickets (Sentry / SigNoz / PostHog / Drizzle / Convex / etc.). Use this ticket as the umbrella for CF-only decisions; do not duplicate CF service evaluations elsewhere.

CF-native tooling roster (single source of truth):
- Compute: Workers, Containers, Durable Objects, Pages
- Storage: R2 (object), KV, D1 (SQLite), DO storage
- Postgres pooling: Hyperdrive (to external Neon/Supabase)
- Async: Queues, Workflows, Pipelines (streaming ingest)
- Data: Analytics Engine, Vectorize
- AI: Workers AI
- Edge / Network: Bot Management, Super Bot Fight Mode, Turnstile, WAF, Email Workers
- Observability: Logpush, Workers Observability / Trace Events
- IaC for CF: see oh-monorepo-fhi (separate ticket; tooling decision spans CF + others)

title: Adopt react-cosmos for component isolation + per-component fixtures
description: Use react-cosmos as the sandbox for evaluating components in @oh/client/ui in isolation. Convention: every component ships at least one fixture; complex components ship multiple covering states + edge cases. Strong MVP candidate for the website tracer.
notes:
Adoption:
- react-cosmos as the dev-time component browser for packages/client/ui.
- Wire into vite-plus dev workflow (cosmos plugin or standalone server).
- Decide: ship cosmos UI behind a route in dev only, OR run as a separate process during dev.

Convention to enforce:
- One *.fixture.tsx per component minimum.
- Complex components: multiple fixtures covering loading / empty / error / saturated / accessibility-edge states.
- Fixtures live next to the component (Component.tsx + Component.fixture.tsx).
- Lint rule (or simple CI check): every exported component in ui/ must have ≥1 sibling fixture.

Workflow:
1) Build component → write fixtures → review in cosmos before wiring into a page.
2) PRs touching a component must update fixtures if props change.
3) Use fixtures as visual-regression input (later: pair with Playwright screenshot tests).

Why react-cosmos vs Storybook:
- Lighter weight, fewer addon ceremonies.
- Fixture-as-prop-snapshot model fits TS-first stack.
- Faster startup; better for the portfolio scale.

Open questions:
- Cosmos config layout in a monorepo (root vs per-package).
- Decorator strategy for context providers (router, auth, theme).
- Integration with Tailwind v4 token loading.
- Story-equivalent for hooks in features/ (cosmos is component-focused; hooks may need a different harness).

title: Pick animation + shader stack (ambient FX without 3D weight)
description: Ship 'fancy' animations cheaply. Default to Paper Shaders for ambient backdrops; reserve react-three-fiber for 3D widgets that earn their weight; Motion/GSAP for everything else.
notes:
Picks (proposed):
- Paper Shaders (paper-design/shaders): premade noise/gradient/wave shaders as React components. Lightest path to fancy backdrops.
- react-three-fiber + drei + @react-three/postprocessing: full 3D + post-FX when a 3D widget or hero scene is justified.
- Motion (formerly framer-motion) OR GSAP: non-shader UI motion (page transitions, micro-interactions). Pick one.
- shader-doodle: Shadertoy-style fragment shaders as a custom element when bringing in pre-existing shaders.

Skipped (for now):
- OGL / REGL: tiny WebGL but hand-roll cost too high for ambient FX.
- Hydra: livecoding overkill for a portfolio site.

Decisions:
- Pick ONE motion lib (Motion vs GSAP). Motion = React-native ergonomics; GSAP = imperative, broader but heavier. Lean Motion unless GSAP-only feature needed.
- Hero/landing FX: Paper Shaders only. No three.js on first paint.

Spike tasks:
- Paper Shaders backdrop on landing page; measure FCP / LCP impact.
- Motion page transition on a route swap.
- (Later) R3F widget: small 3D candle or ribbon visual.

title: Pick chart libraries per surface (price / indicators / dashboards / custom)
description: Choose the chart stack. Plotly stays only where existing perf-tuned charts justify migration. Default to MIT/free libraries with clear per-surface ownership.
notes:
Per-surface picks (proposed):
- Price (OHLCV): TradingView Lightweight Charts. ~45kb, MIT, finance-tuned, candlesticks/area/line/volume.
- Indicators / scanners / dense lines: uPlot. Fastest pure timeseries, MIT, ~45kb.
- Dashboard chrome (KPI cards, simple bar/line): Tremor (Tailwind-native).
- Custom one-offs: Visx (D3 + React primitives) as escape hatch.
- Migrate Plotly: only where it already pays its weight; MIT charts otherwise.

Skipped:
- ECharts: capable but heavier than needed when the above split covers cases.
- Recharts: easy but modest perf; superseded by uPlot + Tremor.
- Highcharts / AG Charts Enterprise: commercial license; skip.

Spike tasks:
- TradingView LC: render OHLCV from DuckDB-WASM result; benchmark zoom/pan p95.
- uPlot: 50k-point indicator line; verify draw time < 16ms.
- Tremor: KPI card + sparkline in dashboard.

Open questions:
- Library theming surface: tokens shared with Tailwind (v4) palette.
- SSR/static-render compatibility (Tanstack Start static).
- Accessibility: keyboard navigation for chart cursors.

title: Adopt Drizzle ecosystem; pick database targets per workload
description: Adopt Drizzle ORM + Kit + Studio as the type-safe SQL layer. Decide which database backs which workload: D1 vs Neon+Hyperdrive vs Turso. Set the migration story.
notes:
Targets to evaluate:
- D1 (CF SQLite): wiki/docs metadata, low-write workloads, simple relational.
- Neon + Hyperdrive: serverless Postgres for richer relational workloads needing transactions, pg-extensions, JSON.
- Turso: SQLite at edge with replication; alt to D1.
- DuckDB: NOT a Drizzle dialect target; analytics layer only (separate ticket).

Repo layout:
- packages/server/db/schema.ts as single source.
- drizzle-kit generate → migrations checked in.
- Apply on deploy: wrangler d1 migrations apply | psql migration.

Workflows:
- Schema-first: edit schema → regenerate types → compiler flags every site to update.
- Drizzle Studio for ad-hoc queries.
- Pair with Better-Auth Drizzle adapter (see auth ticket).

Decision matrix to fill:
| Workload                | Pick   | Why |
| user accounts/sessions  | ?      |     |
| wiki/docs metadata      | ?      |     |
| portfolios/watchlists   | ?      |     |
| scanner results         | ?      |     |
| audit log               | ?      |     |

Open questions:
- D1 row-size + transaction limits acceptable for our writes?
- Hyperdrive setup cost (Neon connection + binding).
- Turso vs D1: replication latency vs CF-native binding ergonomics.

title: Wire Infisical secrets via varlock (lift helpers from chart project)
description: Adopt Infisical as the single source of truth for secrets across local/CI/prod. Lift the safe helpers already used in the private chart project. Skip 1Password entirely.
notes:
Sources:
- Reuse Infisical config patterns + helpers from private chart project (already proven safe).
- Mark items in .env.schema with @sensitive decorator.
- Use varlock Infisical plugin (or exec(infisical secrets get ...) fallback).

Per environment:
- Local dev: Infisical service token in shell; varlock loads via plugin.
- CI (GitHub Actions): Infisical service token as GH Action secret; 'varlock load' validates schema before deploy.
- Prod (CF Workers): sync Infisical → wrangler secrets at deploy time via 'infisical run -- wrangler secret put ...' or CI step. Workers read env bindings; varlock validates at cold start.

Init flow:
1) varlock init  → generate .env.schema from current .env.
2) Annotate sensitive items with @sensitive.
3) Install varlock-infisical plugin.
4) varlock load → verify locally and in CI.
5) Wire Wrangler secret push step in deploy workflow.

Workflows:
- Rotation: rotate in Infisical → CI redeploys with new value → verify via varlock validation.
- New env: copy Infisical project, rotate tokens, deploy.
- Drift detection: nightly varlock load in CI on main → fail on missing.

Open questions:
- Project layout in Infisical (one project per app vs one per repo).
- Path scoping for client-readable vars vs server-only.
- Audit log retention.

title: Adopt PostHog: product analytics + replay + flag provider
description: Stand up PostHog as the analytics backbone and OpenFeature flag provider for the portfolio repo. Reverse-proxied via CF Worker, autocapture off, explicit event taxonomy.
notes:
Setup:
- PostHog Cloud (EU region) or self-host? Decide based on data residency.
- Reverse-proxy via CF Worker route (e.g. /ph) → adblock bypass + first-party cookies.
- Autocapture OFF; explicit capture only (PII risk in finance UI).
- Replay: masking on, sampling 10%, 100% on rage-click / dead-click.
- OpenFeature provider via @openfeature/posthog-provider.

Event taxonomy (initial):
- chart.viewed (symbol, timeframe)
- chart.timeframe_changed (from, to)
- indicator.added (id, params)
- scanner.run (preset_id, result_count)
- portfolio.created / .updated / .deleted

Workflows:
1) Funnel: signup → first chart → first save → D1/D7 return.
2) Cohorts: active scanners, multi-portfolio users, churn risk.
3) Survey: trigger after first scanner run.
4) Group analytics: deferred, for org accounts.
5) Export to R2 parquet for DuckDB analytics later.

Open questions:
- EU vs US cloud (matters if shipping to EU users).
- Self-host cost vs cloud free tier (1M events/month).
- Coordinate with GrowthBook ticket on which flags live where.

title: Adopt Sentry: error monitoring + RUM + interstitial experiment lane
description: Stand up Sentry across apps + workers, with source maps, replay, release health, and a tagged experimental lane for an interstitial / bot-control variant comparison.
notes:
Setup:
- One Sentry project per app (website, gateway, each worker).
- Source-map upload in CI via @sentry/cli, fail-deploy on missing maps.
- Browser SDK with Replay + BrowserTracing + Profiling integrations.
- Tunnel ingest through a CF Worker route (e.g. /_sentry) to bypass adblockers.
- Release tagged with git SHA; deploy webhook → Sentry release API.

Workflows to practise:
1) Triage Discover query (saved): top unresolved by impact.
2) Replay-driven RCA on top issue.
3) Release Health diff between consecutive releases (crash-free %).
4) Sentry Cron monitors for batch + workflow steps.
5) Custom dashboards: frontend errors / backend perf / batch reliability.
6) Spike alerts on event-rate stddev anomaly.

Interstitial / bot-control experimental lane:
- Behind OpenFeature flag (PostHog or GrowthBook provider).
- Variant tag on every Sentry event: interstitial.variant (control/interstitial), interstitial.outcome (passed/challenged/bounced), cf-ray, cf-bot-score.
- Replay 100% on errors, 10% baseline; specifically watch interstitial-path replays.
- Issue alert: errors on /challenge/* > N/5m AND variant=interstitial → notify.
- Custom transaction span around the interstitial detour; track p95.
- Compare Web Vitals (LCP/INP) across variants.
- Goal: quantify disruption cost in error rate + UX deltas.

Open questions:
- Sentry plan tier (free dev / Team / Business)?
- PII scrubbing rules for finance data leaking into stack traces.
- Should interstitial experiment ride on Worker route or app-level redirect?

title: Evaluate auth stack: Better-Auth vs Clerk vs Auth.js (defer WorkOS)

title: Adopt pb33f/openapi-changes for API contract change detection
description: Track OpenAPI spec evolution across commits/branches. Detect breaking vs non-breaking changes, gate releases on breaking changes, generate human-readable changelogs. Pairs with the public-API + Unkey lane.
notes:
Tool: https://github.com/pb33f/openapi-changes
- Diff between two OpenAPI specs (file vs file, git ref vs ref, before/after).
- Classifies changes: breaking / modified / added / removed.
- Outputs: HTML report, JSON, console summary.
- CLI + library; can run in CI.

Adoption plan (when public APIs ship, ties to oh-monorepo-6iu):
- CI step on PRs touching the OpenAPI spec → run openapi-changes against main.
- Fail CI on breaking changes unless PR carries 'api-break' label + version bump.
- Generate HTML report uploaded as PR artifact.
- Auto-comment summary on PR.

Workflows:
1) Pre-merge gate: breaking change blocked without explicit version bump.
2) Release notes: feed openapi-changes output into changelog generation.
3) Consumer notification: when major version bumps, ping Unkey-tracked partners.
4) Spec linting (separate, e.g. spectral) runs alongside.

Open questions:
- Spec source-of-truth: hand-written YAML vs generated from code (orval round-trip vs Hono OpenAPI vs Zod-OpenAPI).
- Versioning policy: URL-versioned (/v1) vs header-versioned.
- Changelog publication target: docs site, README, or external partner portal.

Cross-references:
- oh-monorepo-6iu (Unkey + public APIs) — depends on this for safe iteration.
- oh-monorepo-4e2 (misc eval list, contains orval which generates clients from OpenAPI).

title: Bot / anti-bot research lane (interstitial impact, detection, evasion harness)
description: Stand up a research lane for studying bot detection, interstitial / challenge UX impact, and anti-detection tooling. Feeds the Sentry interstitial experiment with real test traffic. Covers both sides: detection (BotD, fingerprinting) and evasion harness (Patchright, playwright-captcha).
notes:
Detection side:
- Cloudflare Bot Management (paid Pro/Biz/Ent) — production bot scoring.
- Super Bot Fight Mode — free on Pro, basic challenge for definitely-automated traffic.
- Turnstile — free CAPTCHA replacement; embed on key flows.
- BotD (fingerprintjs/BotD) — open-source bot detection in browser; client-side hint, not authoritative.
- WAF custom rules: rate, path, ASN, JA3/JA4 fingerprints.

Evasion / testing harness side:
- Patchright (Kaliiiiiiiiii-Vinyzu/patchright) — patched Playwright to bypass detection; for reproducing bot traffic in tests.
- playwright-captcha (techinz/playwright-captcha) — captcha-handling harness; used to see how challenges fare against scripted clients.
- Use these to GENERATE the test traffic the interstitial experiment needs to learn from.

Cross-link with Sentry interstitial experiment (oh-monorepo-jn4):
- Tag traffic class on every request: human / suspected-bot / known-bot / harness.
- Correlate Sentry error tags w/ bot-score deciles.
- Replay sampling biased toward bordeline scores.

Workflows:
1) Lab harness: Patchright run against staging → capture beacons + Sentry events.
2) Variant rollout: control vs Turnstile vs full interstitial; compare metrics.
3) BotD vs CF Bot Management agreement matrix (where they disagree, why).
4) Quarterly review of CF Bot Management cost vs benefit.

Cross-reference: misc eval ticket oh-monorepo-4e2 already lists patchright + playwright-captcha + BotD repos.

Open questions:
- Ethical/legal scope for evasion testing — only on owned infra.
- Where to store harness traces (R2, retention TTL).
- Whether to expose any of this as a portfolio writeup.

ADDITION: Turnkey (turnkey.com) — evaluate as auth-class challenge for bot control
- Wallet infrastructure-as-code with passkeys + hardware-bound credentials.
- Bot-control angle: hardware-attested passkey challenge as proof-of-humanness, alternative/complement to Turnstile.
- Finance roadmap angle: signed orders, non-custodial wallets, key custody if on-chain finance ever lands.
- Decision: spike alongside Turnstile to compare friction vs assurance.

title: Skill authoring (SkillForge) + skill-perf instrumentation harness
description: Adopt SkillForge's multi-phase methodology for authoring high-quality reusable skills. Build a separate, lightweight perf-instrumentation harness so we can publish iteration data + blog posts about skill performance over time.
notes:
SkillForge (authoring discipline):
- Multi-phase pipeline: triage → 11-lens decompose → XML spec → multi-agent approval.
- Scope is creation/iteration quality gates, NOT performance measurement.
- Adopt for any new skill we publish.

Perf instrumentation gap (separate from SkillForge):
- SkillForge does not measure runtime success / cost / iteration count.
- Need a small custom harness:
  - Each skill emits skill.start / skill.end / skill.outcome events.
  - Properties: skill_id, version, duration_ms, tool_calls, retries, outcome (success / partial / failure), surface (claude code | codex | other).
  - Sink: PostHog (custom event) for funnels + retention; SigNoz span if backend-side.
- Build a simple eval set per skill: golden tasks → automated runs → success rate over time.
- Use this as the data feed for the publishing/blog flow.

Workflow split:
- SkillForge = how you make a skill.
- PostHog/SigNoz events = how you measure it.
- Blog posts = dump of dashboards + reflections + lessons.

Open questions:
- Where does instrumentation live: in each skill SKILL.md as a hook? In a wrapper script that invokes skills? Both?
- Versioning convention for skills (semver-ish; track perf per version).
- Privacy: scrub user-task content from event payloads before sink.
- Publishing pipeline: blog as static MDX in apps/website (when blog ships) or external?

References:
- https://github.com/tripleyak/SkillForge

title: IaC for Cloudflare: Terraform/OpenTofu vs Pulumi (Wrangler-only baseline)
description: Decide IaC tooling for Cloudflare account-level config (zones, DNS, Pages projects, R2 buckets, Queues, Workflows, IAM). Wrangler-only is the baseline; pick a real IaC once >2 services exist.
notes:
Options:
- Wrangler-only: per-Worker config in wrangler.toml. Fine for single-Worker apps. Doesn't cover account/zone/DNS.
- OpenTofu (or Terraform) + cloudflare provider: declarative, mature, broad CF resource coverage.
- Pulumi + @pulumi/cloudflare: TypeScript-native IaC; nice for a TS-first repo. State backend: Pulumi Cloud free tier or self-managed.

Decision matrix to fill:
| Concern              | Wrangler | OpenTofu | Pulumi |
| Zone/DNS records     |  no      | yes      | yes    |
| R2 buckets           |  partial | yes      | yes    |
| Queues/Workflows     |  yes     | yes      | yes    |
| Pages projects       |  partial | yes      | yes    |
| TS-native            |  n/a     | no (HCL) | yes    |
| State management     |  none    | required | required |
| Drift detection      |  no      | yes      | yes    |

Rec to validate:
- Pulumi for new things (TS-native fits the repo voice).
- OpenTofu fallback if Pulumi state cost gets noisy.
- Wrangler stays for per-Worker config (no IaC migration tax there).

Workflows:
- IaC repo or co-located in oh-monorepo (tools/iac)?
- Plan-on-PR / Apply-on-merge gate via GH Actions.
- Secrets pulled from Infisical at apply time (no plain-text in state).

Open questions:
- State backend: Pulumi Cloud free vs S3-on-R2 + locking.
- Multi-env (dev/staging/prod) shape: workspaces vs stacks.
- Bootstrapping order: account → zones → services.

title: Spike Convex vs Drizzle+Durable Objects for reactive metadata layer
description: OHLCV stays on R2/DuckDB. Reactive metadata (portfolios, watchlists, scanner results, relative-strength rankings, aggregate measures) needs its own layer. Benchmark Convex vs Drizzle + Durable Object websocket broadcaster.
notes:
Workloads in scope:
- Portfolios (CRUD, share/collab).
- Watchlists.
- Scanner runs (input config + cached output).
- Relative-strength rankings (periodically recomputed).
- Aggregate measures across multiple charts.
- Alerts and notifications.

Out of scope: OHLCV history (R2 + DuckDB).

Option A: Convex
- Reactive queries → live UI without websocket plumbing.
- Scheduled fns → periodic recompute.
- File storage → cached scanner snapshots.
- Subscriptions → portfolio sharing.
- Pulls infra off Cloudflare; platform split.

Option B: Drizzle (D1 or Neon+Hyperdrive) + Durable Object websocket broadcaster
- Stays on Cloudflare.
- More plumbing: change-feed → DO fanout → client subscription.
- Owns its data; no platform lock-in.

Spike plan:
- Build the same scanner-run + portfolio-share feature in both.
- Compare: dev velocity, latency p95 on subscription updates, cost projection at 1k/10k MAU, ops burden.
- Decide based on UX margin vs platform-split cost.

Boundary discipline (whichever wins):
- Convex client (or DO RPC client) lives ONLY in @oh/client/features/<metadata-feature>.
- OHLCV-touching code never imports it.

Open questions:
- Convex's hosting region(s) acceptable for EU data residency?
- DO storage limits per object for our largest aggregate.
- Migration cost out of Convex if it doesn't pan out.

title: Spike DuckDB-WASM local-first analytics behind login
description: Prototype the local-first analytics lane: server signs short-lived URLs to scoped R2 parquet files; browser DuckDB-WASM queries them. Server holds metadata only. Validate latency, payload size, and query ergonomics for OHLCV + indicators.
notes:
Pattern:
1) User authenticates (Better-Auth).
2) Server signs short-lived presigned URLs to R2 parquet scoped to user.
3) Browser loads @duckdb/duckdb-wasm + apache-arrow.
4) httpfs attaches signed URLs.
5) All chart queries / indicator computations run in browser.
6) Server only sees metadata (Convex/Drizzle); no query content leaves client.

Spike goals:
- Cold-load size budget: <2 MB JS + <5 MB initial parquet for one symbol/year.
- Query p95 < 200ms for typical indicator span on 5y daily OHLCV.
- Partition strategy benchmark: per-symbol-per-year vs row-group-by-day.
- Lazy-load chunks on timeframe pan/zoom.

Risks:
- DuckDB-WASM bundle size on cold start.
- HTTP range request granularity (parquet row-groups must align).
- Service worker caching strategy.
- CORS on R2 signed URLs.

Open questions:
- Where to source initial OHLCV (own ingest pipeline vs vendor)?
- Encryption at rest in R2 (CF-managed) acceptable for portfolio/personal?
- Should there be a server-side fallback for huge cross-symbol scans?

Cross-references:
- depends on R2 + Better-Auth + Drizzle.
- feeds into chart picks (TradingView LC, uPlot).

title: Adopt SigNoz for backend traces + metrics + logs (OTel-native)
description: Stand up self-hosted SigNoz as the OTel-native observability stack for backend services (gateway, batch processors, event workers). Bridge trace IDs with Sentry so frontend errors link to backend spans.
notes:
Setup:
- Self-host SigNoz via docker compose (ClickHouse + Query + Frontend).
- OTel collector deployed alongside; OTLP receivers for HTTP + gRPC.
- Every service emits OTLP traces + metrics + logs.
- Pino logger with otel-pino-transport for log → SigNoz pipeline.
- Sentry ↔ OTel bridge: include sentry trace ID in spans (and vice versa).

Dashboards (initial):
- RED per service (Rate / Errors / Duration).
- USE per resource (Util / Sat / Errors) for ClickHouse + Workers.
- Queue depth + consumer lag (CF Queues exporter).
- Workflow step latency (each step a span).
- Indicator computation duration p95 by symbol.

Alerts:
- Burn-rate-style SLO alerts (multi-window).
- Queue lag > N for > M minutes.
- Trace error-rate per service.

Workflows:
1) Slow-trace drill: TraceQL → spans → DB call → fix.
2) Service map review weekly.
3) ClickHouse query optimisation (transferable skill for timeseries roadmap).

Boundary with Sentry:
- Sentry: errors, replays, releases (frontend + node).
- SigNoz: traces, infra metrics, logs (backend + workers).
- Bridge via shared trace IDs.

Open questions:
- ClickHouse hosting: self-managed vs ClickHouse Cloud.
- Retention policy for logs vs traces vs metrics.
- Cost trajectory at expected ingest volume.

title: Wire OpenFeature + GrowthBook for stats-rigorous experimentation
description: Adopt OpenFeature as the vendor-neutral flag SDK. Use GrowthBook as the experimentation provider; pair with PostHog as the data source. Define which provider owns which flag class.
notes:
Adoption plan:
- @openfeature/web-sdk + @openfeature/server-sdk in apps and workers.
- GrowthBook self-host (Docker compose, Mongo) OR cloud free tier.
- GrowthBook reads events from PostHog (datasource integration).
- Edge SDK eval inside CF Worker → no roundtrip flag eval.

Provider split:
- PostHog flags  → marketing/UX/cohort-targeted rollouts.
- GrowthBook    → A/B/n experiments with statistical readout.
- Same flag → ONE provider only. Document the boundary.

Workflows:
1) Pre-experiment power calc (MDE, sample size, runtime).
2) Guardrail metrics: error rate, p95 latency. Auto-stop on breach.
3) Holdback: small permanent control to detect long-term drift.
4) Flag hygiene: naming feat.<area>.<name>, owner tag, kill date in description; monthly stale-flag sweep.
5) Bayesian readout: stop on win-prob > 95% AND MDE met.

Open questions:
- GrowthBook self-host vs cloud — operating burden vs control.
- How OpenFeature client is provided in @oh/client (singleton vs per-feature).
- Default targeting: user_id vs anonymous_id stability.
